subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What good comes from the lovers' deaths at the play's close?
options: The Prince seizes both family estates
Verona is freed from the plague
questions.explain: The grieving families finally end their feud, reconciled by the tragedy they caused.

questions.q: Why is the theme of witchcraft especially significant in the Jacobean context of Macbeth?
options: King James I was deeply interested in witchcraft and wrote a book, Daemonologie
Witchcraft was illegal to depict on stage
The Pope had recently endorsed witch-hunts
Shakespeare himself was tried for witchcraft
questions.explain: James I wrote Daemonologie and believed in witches, so the supernatural would have unsettled his court.

questions.q: What does the recurring imagery of blood most strongly symbolise in Macbeth?
options: Inescapable guilt and the consequences of murder
questions.explain: Blood that cannot be washed away, from Macbeth's hands to Lady Macbeth's "damned spot", represents unshakeable guilt.

questions.q: What does Macbeth famously call life in his despairing speech after Lady Macbeth's death?
options: "A tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury"
questions.explain: He calls life "a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing", showing his nihilistic despair.

questions.q: How is the prophecy about Birnam Wood ultimately fulfilled?
options: Malcolm's soldiers cut branches as camouflage as they advance
questions.explain: Malcolm's army cuts boughs from Birnam Wood to disguise their numbers, so the wood appears to move on Dunsinane.

questions.q: In Macbeth, which title does Macbeth already hold at the very start of the play, before any prophecy is fulfilled?
questions.explain: Macbeth begins the play as Thane of Glamis, his inherited title, before the witches greet him as Cawdor and king.

questions.q: How does Tybalt's character drive the play's theme of love versus hate?
options: His fierce hatred of the Montagues fuels the violence that dooms the lovers
questions.explain: Tybalt's aggressive hatred of Montagues sparks the duel that kills Mercutio and gets Romeo banished.

questions.q: Mr Birling's confident speeches about the Titanic being "unsinkable" are an example of what dramatic technique?
questions.explain: The audience knows the Titanic sank, making Birling's claims ironic and undermining his judgement.

questions.q: What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to do to her so she can help commit murder?
options: To "unsex" her and fill her with cruelty
To protect her husband in battle
To give her the gift of prophecy
questions.explain: She cries "unsex me here", asking to be stripped of feminine compassion to carry out the killing.

questions.q: How old is Juliet in the play, reflecting Elizabethan attitudes to marriage?
questions.explain: Juliet is not yet fourteen, and her father pushes an early marriage, reflecting period customs around young brides.

questions.q: What dramatic device does Shakespeare use in the Prologue when it calls Romeo and Juliet 'a pair of star-crossed lovers'?
questions.explain: The Prologue foreshadows the lovers' doomed, fated deaths from the outset.

questions.q: How does Mrs Birling's response to the Inspector reveal her prejudice?
options: She looks down on Eva as a girl of a lower class undeserving of help
questions.explain: Mrs Birling dismisses Eva as a member of the lower classes and refuses her charity, exposing her snobbery.

questions.q: In Jacobean England, the reigning monarch when Macbeth was written claimed descent from which character in the play?
questions.explain: James I traced his lineage to Banquo, which is why the witches show Banquo's descendants as future kings.

questions.q: What is the name of the young woman whose death the Inspector investigates?
questions.explain: The dead girl is Eva Smith, who also went by the name Daisy Renton.

questions.q: In Romeo and Juliet, which character urges calm and tries to keep the peace, refusing to fight Tybalt before Mercutio intervenes?
questions.explain: Romeo refuses to fight the newly-related Tybalt, prompting Mercutio to duel in his place.

questions.q: What does the murder of a king represent in the play's idea of kingship and the divine right of kings?
options: A crime against the natural and divine order
questions.explain: Killing Duncan, God's anointed king, violates the divine order, reflected in the unnatural disturbances that follow.

questions.q: In Romeo and Juliet, at whose party do Romeo and Juliet first meet?
questions.explain: Romeo gatecrashes the Capulets' masked ball, where he meets Juliet and instantly falls in love.

questions.q: Why does Macbeth have Banquo murdered after becoming king?
options: The witches prophesied Banquo's descendants would be kings
questions.explain: The witches foretold Banquo would father a line of kings, so Macbeth fears him and orders his death.

questions.q: How does Lady Macbeth die?
options: She apparently takes her own life
questions.explain: Her death is reported and understood to be suicide, the consequence of overwhelming guilt.

questions.q: What does Priestley imply by having each family member tied to the same girl?
options: That the actions of individuals combine to cause real harm to others
That only Mr Birling is to blame
questions.explain: The chain of linked actions shows how everyone's choices contributed to Eva's downfall, reinforcing collective responsibility.

questions.q: What central message does Inspector Goole deliver about society?
options: That the rich deserve their wealth
That "we are members of one body" and responsible for one another
That the law solves all problems
questions.explain: The Inspector argues people are responsible for each other, the play's theme of social responsibility.

questions.q: Who kills Mercutio in the play?
questions.explain: Tybalt fatally stabs Mercutio under Romeo's arm, prompting Mercutio's curse "A plague o' both your houses!".
